title: Ordered sets: comparison, bounds, and quotients

based_on.title: Mathematical foundations: (3) Lattice theory — Part I
A lattice-theoretical fixpoint theorem and its applications

summary: Compare elements in partial orders, distinguish extrema from bounds, and turn a preorder into an ordered set of classes.
abstract: Two sets can be incomparable under inclusion, just as neither of the positive integers two and three divides the other. Partial orders let us study such comparisons without requiring every pair to be comparable. Among subsets of a fixed set, unions are least upper bounds and intersections are greatest lower bounds. These bounds have a striking consequence: any map from a power set to itself that preserves inclusion has a subset it leaves unchanged, with a least and a greatest such subset. The Knaster–Tarski theorem extends this fixed-point result to every complete lattice, an ordered set where all collections have both kinds of bound.
